title: Little Hawley Rising Anew
premise: Silas Crane, Hawley's meticulous estate lawyer, is retained by a dying woman who pays him to prove that her son's murder — scheduled, she insists, for the night of the autumn gala — will never happen. When the young man turns up dead exactly as predicted, Silas realizes his client engineered the prophecy to force him, the keeper of every town secret in his filing cabinets, into the open. As he traces a decade of documents he himself notarized, Silas uncovers a conspiracy among Hawley's founding families to bury an old death and frame an outsider. In the end, Silas sacrifices his invisibility and his law license, springing the trap at the preliminary hearing so the true killer — the town's beloved patriarch — confesses on the record before the trial can be steered away from the truth.
about_author: Odile Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent years cataloguing probate files in New England and never stopped wondering what the quietest clients were hiding. She writes mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the people who believe order can hold back the dark.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Silas Crane. A frail stranger, Margaret Voss, retains Silas to prove her son Daniel will NOT be murdered at the autumn gala, paying triple his fee upfront. Her certainty unnerves him; her file contains a date, a method, and a name redacted in his own handwriting from ten years ago. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas searches his archive for the Voss name and finds a gap where a 2014 file should be — a gap only he could have made. His clerk, Junie, notices him rattled for the first time in a decade. Beat: the archivist discovers his own archive has been edited against him.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas canvasses old colleagues: Sheriff Dane Whitlock deflects, matriarch Eleanor Ashcombe offers tea and veiled warnings, and Daniel Voss himself seems oddly resigned, as if expecting something. Beat: isolation — everyone knows more than they'll say.

chapters.title: The Gala Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas secures an invitation to the Ashcombe autumn gala by offering to update Eleanor's will. He observes the founding families' choreography of power and spots Daniel arriving uninvited, pale and determined. Beat: foreboding beneath candlelight and civility.

chapters.title: Murder, As Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the gala, the lights fail for ninety seconds; when they return, Daniel Voss is dead at the boathouse, exactly as Margaret predicted. Silas finds his own ten-year-old notary stamp pressed into the mud beside the body. Beat: horror — the prophecy fulfilled and implicating him.

chapters.title: Person of Interest
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Sheriff Whitlock, under pressure from the selectmen, names Silas a person of interest: he predicted the death, he was present, his stamp is there. Junie urges him to run; instead he opens Margaret's retainer agreement and finds clause seven — 'payment contingent on truth surfacing.' Beat: cornered but committed.

chapters.title: What Margaret Knew
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas visits Margaret's care facility and finds her room emptied; nurses say her son moved her out weeks ago — though Daniel died childless of secrets. A hidden letter tells Silas: 'You filed it. You know where.' Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The 2014 File
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Following his own past habits, Silas reconstructs the missing 2014 file from cross-references: a drowning ruled accidental, a witness paid off, and a settlement drafted by his own hand for the Ashcombes. The drowned man was Margaret's husband. Beat: complicity — he was the machine all along.

chapters.title: Junie's Discovery
chapters.summary: POV Junie Okafor. Left alone with the archive, Junie finds a duplicate key log showing someone accessed the vault three nights running — someone with Silas's old after-hours code, retired two years ago. Beat: loyalty tested; she chooses to tell Silas rather than the sheriff.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Tea
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Eleanor Ashcombe invites Silas for tea and offers him immunity, reputation, partnership — if he simply certifies the estate and stops asking questions. She speaks of Hawley as a living thing that must be protected. Beat: temptation; power's velvet voice.

chapters.title: The Outsider
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The police arrest a drifter, Cole Mercer, for Daniel's murder — a man whose alibi is a bus ticket Silas realizes was purchased with Ashcombe trust funds. Silas faces a choice: stay invisible or become Mercer's advocate. He signs on as defense counsel. Beat: crossing the line.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's File
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Comparing the murder scene report to his own memory of the 2014 file, Silas sees the staging mirrors the old drowning too precisely — the killer learned from the same documents he drafted. Only four people ever saw those pages. Beat: the hunt narrows.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas confronts Sheriff Whitlock, who admits he was ordered to close the 2014 case but swears he's kept the original evidence locked away since — evidence someone recently tried to buy. Whitlock agrees to help, then goes silent and requests a transfer. Beat: ally lost to fear.

chapters.title: Margaret Returns
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Margaret Voss surfaces at a motel outside town, having staged her own disappearance to watch who moved. She reveals she hired Silas because he was the only man honest enough to keep records — and therefore the only one who could read them back. Beat: purpose revealed; the client becomes the guide.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Of the four who saw the 2014 file, one is dead (Daniel), one is bought (Whitlock), one is power itself (Eleanor) — and the fourth is Eleanor's son, Julian Ashcombe, the town prosecutor who will try Mercer's case. Beat: the trap takes shape around the courtroom.

chapters.title: Framing the Frame
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas and Junie quietly rebuild the 2014 file: certified copies, the payment ledger, and a deposition from the paid witness, now dying and willing to talk. They plan to enter it all at the preliminary hearing, forcing Julian to respond on the record. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Someone ransacks the office; Junie hides the reconstructed file in a probate box labeled with a deceased client's name. She is followed home and offered money, then threats. Beat: fear endured; the loyal apprentice becomes a co-conspirator for truth.

chapters.title: The Hearing Begins
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the preliminary hearing, Julian prosecutes with polished confidence while Silas, defending Mercer, lays his paper trail piece by piece. The gallery shifts; Eleanor watches from the front row like a chess player. Beat: rising tension — every move now public.

chapters.title: Checkmate in Open Court
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas introduces the 2014 settlement bearing Julian's signature as trustee, then plays a recording — Margaret's phone call to Julian weeks earlier, in which he references details only the killer would know. Julian's composure cracks on the record. Beat: climax; the trap springs.

chapters.title: Confession Before the Trial
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Facing disbarment-worthy exposure and his mother's legacy burning down, Julian confesses to both deaths — his father's drowning in 2014 and Daniel's murder — believing the trial could still be managed, not knowing the transcript is already sealed. Beat: catharsis; corruption undone by its own confidence.

chapters.title: The Price of Visibility
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In the aftermath, Silas surrenders his law license for his role in the 2014 cover-up, accepting the bar's judgment even as the town owes him its cleansing. Eleanor resigns in disgrace; Whitlock testifies; Mercer walks free. Beat: bittersweet accountability.

chapters.title: Little Hawley Rising Anew
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Months later, Silas keeps a smaller office doing pro bono work, his archive finally honest. Margaret visits with flowers for Daniel's grave; Junie studies for the bar herself. The town begins, imperfectly, to remember everything. Beat: belonging earned through truth, not silence.
